methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements that capture a single aspect of the system's functionality or design. For the original research topic, this meant extracting individual statements about the FSM's behavior, inputs, outputs, and reset conditions. For the generated specification, this involved identifying the specific logic functions, timing considerations, and interface behaviors described.
mindtraced_atomic_units: FSM starts in reset state A
FSM remains in state A while s = 0
FSM transitions to state B when s = 1
In state B, FSM examines input w over next three clock cycles
If w = 1 in exactly two of the three cycles, output z is set to 1 in the subsequent clock cycle
FSM prepares to evaluate the next three w inputs after setting z
Design should use the minimum number of states
Reset input is active high and synchronous
s input is used only in state A
Consider just the w input after state A
The problem description does not specify how the FSM returns to state A after it has entered state B
spec_atomic_units: Output z is asserted if and only if w is 1 in exactly two out of the next three clock cycles after transitioning to state B (s=1)
Otherwise, z is 0
Combinational logic block monitors w input over a three-cycle window
z = (w1 & w2 & ~w3) | (w1 & ~w2 & w3) | (~w1 & w2 & w3) (Boolean function for z)
Combinational logic is active only after FSM has transitioned to state B (s=1)
z = s & ((w1 & w2 & ~w3) | (w1 & ~w2 & w3) | (~w1 & w2 & w3)) (Complete combinational logic function for z)
Implementation should use AND, OR, and NOT gates
FSM transitions from state A to state B when s transitions from 0 to 1
w1, w2, and w3 represent the value of w in the first, second, and third clock cycles, respectively, after the transition to state B
clk input is the clock signal
reset input, when high, synchronously resets the FSM to its initial state A
s input triggers the transition from state A to state B when s is 1
w input is sampled in state B over three clock cycles to determine the value of the output z
z is updated on the clock edge following the three clock cycles of w sampling
critical path involves the clk to z delay
reset signal must be asserted long enough before the rising edge of clk to ensure a proper reset
s input must be stable before the rising edge of clk to ensure correct state transition from A to B
w input must be stable before the rising edge of clk during the three clock cycles it is being sampled
output z is a registered output
FSM transitions on the positive edge of the clk signal
